Excessive hand scraping

Diaphragms and Nozzle Plates
 as shown in 
figure 3

Diaphragms and nozzle 
plates when removed from shell must be blast cleaned using aluminum oxide 220 
mesh or finer. Special attention should be paid to the following areas, steam 
paths radial fits, crush pins, packing fits, joints, support blocks, lower 
center line centering pin fits and all steam sealing areas after blast cleaning, 
it may be necessary to hone all fits prior to reassembly.

On diaphragm partition and 
nozzle partitions that are eroded thin on the trailing edges, it is possible to 
roll the trailing edges over by excessive blast cleaning. This should be avoided 
and brought to the blast cleaner operators attention before any blasting takes 
place. After the blast cleaning process is completed, a through cleaning with 
compressed air is imperative.

Bolt Threads, Tapped Holes, 
Dowels and Fits Unit

Bolt threads should be cleaned using approved solvents and wire brushes. After a 
through cleaning with solvents and wire brushes, a die nut should be run over 
the threads, if one is available.

All tapped holes 
(horizontal joints on LP sections, nozzle areas, diaphragm horizontal joints and 
packing casing fits) should be cleaned with approved solvents. A good tap should 
be run inside to clean up threads. After tapping and cleaning, holes should be 
covered to avoid contamination and damage to internal threads.

All dowels and dowel fits 
should be cleaned with solvents and lightly polished with a very fit grit emery 
cloth. Avoid removal of any dowel or dowel fit metal, this will cause a loose 
fit.

All nuts should be cleaned 
with solvents and wire brush and then a good top should be run through each nut 
to ensure good threads.

Oil deflectors should be 
cleaned, using wire brushes and solvents sealing surfaces and horizontal joints 
should be game over lightly with a hone stone to remove any high spots or burrs.
Bearing Journal Surfaces and Thrust Runners

Wash Journal surfaces with 
a solvent and then strap lap with 400 grit or finer emery cloth rolls. The rolls 
can be purchased in 2 inch widths and are approximately 50 yards long.

Follow this procedure to 
strap lap the journal. Pull with left hand and allow the right hand to go 
towards the rotor while keeping the emery cloth snug, then reverse the procedure 
move back and forth over total journal surface until the total area is strapped 
satisfactorily. Always keep even force on the strapping cloth to ensure even 
polishing.

Wash the thrust runner with 
solvents and polish out any rough spots with a hard Arkansas stone, using radial 
movements. If a slight rusting or sludge build up is present. It is acceptable 
to clean with scotch bright pads and solvents .12 - horizontal, vertical and all 
other metal to metal sealing surfaces. Wash with solvent and use 
scotch bright industrial pads to remove dirt and oil residue. After cleaning 
thoroughly, go over all surfaces with a good grade, medium hardness hone stone 
to remove any nicks.

Gasket areas, including 
steam lead pipes and manhole covers need thorough cleaning using a putty knife, 
wire wheel mounted on air grinder, or side grinder, and hand honing to give 
goad sealing surfaces after cleaning you should immediate coat with some type of 
preservative to prevent corrosion and rust. It is unnecessary to clean twice.

Steam Leak off Piping, Hydraulic Oil Piping Mechanical 
Hydraulic Control 'MHC', and Stainless Steel Tubing Electro Hydraulic Control 'EHC'

The steam leak off piping 
should be blown through to ensure that it is open. Hydraulic oil piping 
internals should be washed in solvent and blown through with dry air to ensure 
that they are clean. Stainless steel tubing internals should be washed with 
enraptured alcohol to ensure clean lines after cleaning all piping and tubing, 
the ends should be closed to prevent contamination.

After the blast cleaning 
process has been completed, you must blow out dust and residue from the rotor, 
diaphragms, inner shells, nozzles and packing casing (using dray air supply). 
You should lubricate all journals, metal to metal fits, couplings and any other 
surfaces which you do not want to rust or corrode. Journals and diaphragm 
partitions should be covered or stored in areas to prevent damage from occurring 
to them.
